body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Saturday, August 22, 2026 — a hot one with a high near 103°, and air quality is moderate. Our top story this morning is a deadly shooting at an Independence High School football game that left the neighborhood shaken and a 15-year-old suspect arrested. Overnight, we had a shooting at a Taco Bell on Baker Street, a fire at a vacant house on King Street, and a two-vehicle collision with one car on fire at Gosford and Harris. Let’s get you caught up.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious call came just after midnight with a shooting reported at a Taco Bell in the Baker Street area. A witness told officers they saw someone shot, and the suspect was described as a white male in his 40s to 50s wearing a black shirt and dark pants, sitting inside a white vehicle — possibly a Ford Explorer. Officers responded with an officer-safety broadcast. Before that, around 2:16 a.m., flames were visible inside a vacant single-story house on King Street with heavy smoke showing. Multiple engines and a truck company responded, and the fire was under control by about 2:25. Just before 11 p.m., a two-vehicle collision left one vehicle on fire near Gosford Road and Harris Road. Engine 14 and Engine 9 responded — one car was smoking with another about a quarter mile back — and command dubbed it the Harris Incident. Injuries were unknown. Multiple reports of a grass fire drew a large response — engines, patrol units, a water tender, a dozer and a helicopter — around 10:30 p.m. southbound on Highway 395 north of Brown Road. Crews found a small roadside fire that was quickly extinguished, and the extra equipment was canceled. Around 10:38 p.m., an assault with a knife was reported with no injuries. The suspect — about 6 feet tall with neck tattoos, wearing black shorts, a gray shirt and white shoes — fled on foot northbound.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 103° and a low around 75° tonight. It’s currently 97° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is moderate.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that McFarland police are investigating a homicide after a 26-year-old man was shot and killed Saturday afternoon at the Capri Laundromat in the 100 block of Perkins Avenue.** Officers responded to the scene at approximately 3:18 p.m. and found the man suffering from multiple gunshot wounds inside the laundromat. Officers immediately provided medical aid and initiated CPR, but the victim was pronounced dead at the scene. Preliminary information indicates two unknown suspects arrived at the Capri Liquors in the 100 block of Perkins Avenue and confronted the victim inside the Capri Laundromat, which is adjacent to the gas pumps. An argument led to one of the suspects producing a firearm and shooting the victim multiple times. The two suspects then fled the area in an unknown vehicle. No suspects have been identified, no arrests have been made, and the motive remains unknown. The victim’s identity will be released after next of kin have been notified. McFarland Police Department detectives are actively working the scene and gathering investigative information. Police say there is no current threat to the community, but the public is advised to avoid the area until the scene is processed.

**KGET 17 tells us that Bakersfield Mayor Karen Goh released a statement on the deadly shooting at Independence High School.** Mayor Goh expressed her condolences to the victim’s family and friends and urged anyone with information to come forward. She emphasized that the safety of our community is a top priority and that the city is working closely with law enforcement to ensure justice is served. The mayor’s statement comes after a 15-year-old suspect was arrested in connection to the shooting.

**According to Bakersfield Now, Southwest Market canceled its Saturday event at Independence High School after the fatal shooting.** Organizers said the decision was made out of respect for the victim’s family and to allow the community time to heal. The event was expected to feature local vendors, food trucks, and live music. No word yet on whether it will be rescheduled.

## Something good

A local family is organizing a flea market to help cover the cost of a prosthetic leg for Villafana. The event aims to raise $8,900 to support this important cause. It’s a heartwarming example of our community coming together to help one of our own.

## Coming up this week

On Wednesday, August 26, the Bakersfield City Council will hold a Special City Council Meeting at 12:00 p.m. followed by a City Council Meeting at 3:30 p.m. and another at 5:15 p.m. All meetings will be held at City Hall. Also this week, the Fox Theater has a full lineup of events: Los Yonic’s Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio will perform tonight, Saturday, August 22. On Tuesday, August 25, Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027 goes on sale. Rodney Carrington takes the stage on Thursday, August 27. CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE is set for Friday, August 28. And on Saturday, August 29, Willie Barcena and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix will perform. Be sure to check the Fox Theater’s website for tickets and more information.
